Raj: Heads-up — spotted a sharp drop in prefix cache hit rate for model redwood-sea-13b on the per-route panel. /assist/code is the worst: token_savings down ~45% for tenant acme. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/obs/dash/0x8c :eyes:
infra-bot: ALERT: metric 'prefix-cache.hitrate' dropped >30% on route '/assist/code' model 'redwood-sea-13b' at 2026-03-18T02:10Z. Ticket INF-2891 auto-created.
Kevin: I rolled auto-kernel-v2 and bumped continuous-batching.threshold -> 12 last night across canary. Could be related. :thinking_face:
Maria: We also merged prompt-key normalization PR (#412) that strips punctuation and normalizes whitespace before keying. That will change keys and collisions — deployed 01:58 UTC. :warning:
Elaine: Quick check — did the KV cache warmup run for acme? warmup-runner logs show failures around 02:14 UTC.
Elaine: ```
warmup-runner[02:14:07]: batch=42 tenant=acme status=failed error=504 upstream timeout
warmup-runner[02:14:08]: retry 1/3
```
Oliver: I profiled the runtime over the window. The kernel switch increased avg latency ~6ms which reduced batching opportunities. Fewer coalesced requests -> fewer prefix matches during aggregation. Quick numbers: avg_latency_ms: before=18 after=24; effective_batch_size: before=6.2 after=3.1.
Kevin: If batch size collapsed we lose the amortized prefix checks that surface hits. Can we correlate per-tenant batching distribution (acme vs others)? :mag:
Maria: Running a fast query on telemetry to slice by tenant now — will post results.
Maria: ```sql
SELECT tenant, avg(batch_size) as avg_bs, p50(latency_ms) as p50_ms
FROM runtime.batching
WHERE model = 'redwood-sea-13b' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-18T01:30Z' AND '2026-03-18T02:30Z'
GROUP BY tenant
ORDER BY avg_bs DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
Raj: Action items: 1) Rollback auto-kernel-v2 on canary (I'll take it) 2) Re-run warmup for acme 3) Add temporary alert: per-tenant avg_batch_size < 4. Also add a 'tokens saved / 1k req' panel with tenant filter to the hit-rate dashboard.
infra-bot: Ticket INF-2891 assigned to Kevin, Maria. See https://issues.redwood/INF-2891
Kevin: Reverted kernel selection on canary. Posting status in 5m. :thumbsup:
Kevin: Canary revert shows batch_size recovering to ~5.6, hit_rate trending up. Monitoring for 30m.
Raj: Nice. After stabilization let's add a small panel that shows token-saved delta vs pre-change baseline + add a per-model per-route sparkline so regressions like this are visible at-a-glance. :memo:
